leads.title: Constitution of the Republic of Moldova - marriage definition
leads.documents: Legal status baseline that same-sex marriage/civil unions are not recognized; marriage explicitly defined as between a man and a woman.
leads.detail: No URL visible in provided text; cited as 'Moldovan Constitution explicitly defines marriage as being between a man and a woman' and referenced in 23 May 2013 propaganda-related bill discussion re Constitution and Family Code

leads.title: Moldovan Parliament Anti-Discrimination Law on sexual orientation in employment (2012)
leads.documents: Adoption of workplace discrimination ban on basis of sexual orientation; key employment protection for LGBTQ workers.
leads.detail: No URL visible in provided text; detail visible: adopted by Parliament 25 May 2012, signed by President Nicolae Timofti 28 May 2012, took effect 1 January 2013; lobbied by GenderDoc-M coalition

leads.title: Codul serviciilor media audiovizuale al Republicii Moldova, Article 11
leads.documents: Media law ban on discrimination/propaganda of hatred based on sexual orientation by audiovisual broadcasters.
leads.detail: No URL visible in provided text; detail visible: so-called 'media propaganda law' entered into force 1 January 2019, Article 11 prohibits 'propagating incitement, promotion or justification of racial hatred, xenophobia, anti-Semitism or other forms of hatred founded on intolerance or discrimination based on sex, race, nationality, religion, disability or sexual orientation'

leads.title: Parliament of Moldova Law No.2 (2023)
leads.documents: Expansion of anti-discrimination protections to include sexual orientation and gender identity against 'any kind of discrimination' - directly relevant to trans legal protection.
leads.detail: No URL visible in provided text; detail visible: passed in 2023 as Law No.2 (2023)

leads.title: European Court of Human Rights - 2012 ruling against Moldova over 2008 Pride ban
leads.documents: Court finding that Moldovan authorities violated human rights by cancelling/banning 2008 Moldova Pride; documents enforcement of freedom of assembly for LGBTQ events and police failure to protect.
leads.detail: No URL visible in provided text; detail visible: 2008 event in Chisinau banned evening before by Mayor Dorin Chirtoaca, police stood by during attacks 11 May 2008; ECHR ruled in 2012 violation; criticized internationally including by British Foreign Secretary David Miliband

leads.title: Moldovan court decision of 20 June 2013 on Gagauzia propaganda law
leads.documents: Invalidation of Gagauzia regional ban on 'propaganda' of homosexuality, bisexuality and transness, bans on LGBT organization registration and clubs; holds violations of freedom of speech and human rights.
leads.detail: No URL visible in provided text; detail visible: Gagauzia Parliament approved bill 30 April 2013 without administrative sanctions/fines; invalidated 20 June 2013

leads.title: ILGA-Europe Rainbow Europe ranking reports
leads.documents: Institutional human-rights benchmarking of Moldova LGBT legislation; last of 49 European countries in 2012 rising to 23rd place by 2023 due to expanded sexual orientation and gender identity protections.
leads.detail: No URL visible in provided text; detail visible: ILGA-Europe ranked Moldova last in list of 49 in 2012, 23rd place by 2023

leads.title: Ministry of Health of Moldova - official letter on homosexuality
leads.documents: Government health authority position that homosexuality is not considered a disease and medical services accessible regardless of sexual orientation; relevant to trans/visitor health access claims.
leads.detail: No URL visible in provided text; detail visible: described as official letter communicated after 1995 decriminalization

leads.title: Pew Research Center - May 2017 Eastern European countries survey
leads.documents: Public-attitudes data on social acceptance risk: 92% of Moldovans said homosexuality should not be accepted, 88% among 18-34, 5% supported same-sex marriage.
leads.detail: No URL visible in provided text; detail visible: Pew Research Center survey in Eastern European countries, May 2017

leads.title: United Nations Human Rights Council - June 2011 SOGI resolution vote
leads.documents: Moldova state action on international LGBTQ rights machinery; used its HRC seat to vote against first successful UN resolution condemning discrimination/violence based on sexual orientation and gender identity.
leads.detail: No URL visible in provided text; detail visible: June 2011 vote
